scenario: Greeting someone for the first time
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; used for identity, state, and characteristics.
Used to ask and say one's name.
Expression of gratitude; also functions as the verb 'danken'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Guten Tag! Ich heiße Anna. Und du?
dialogue.translation: Good day! My name is Anna. And you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hallo Anna! Ich heiße Peter. Freut mich sehr!
dialogue.translation: Hello Anna! My name is Peter. Nice to meet you!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Freut mich auch. Wie geht es dir?
dialogue.translation: Nice to meet you too. How are you?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Danke, gut! Und dir?
dialogue.translation: Thanks, fine! And you?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mir geht es auch gut. Schön, dich kennenzulernen!
dialogue.translation: I'm fine too. Nice to meet you!

scenario: Asking where something is in a store
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Irregular verb, used with 'nicht' for 'not to know'.
Modal particle used in questions to make them more colloquial: 'Wo ist denn...?' = 'Where is... then?'

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entschuldigung, wo finde ich hier die Milch?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, where do I find the milk here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Die Milch ist dort hinten, ja.
dialogue.translation: The milk is back there, yes.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Und wo ist denn der Käse?
dialogue.translation: And where is the cheese then?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ich weiß nicht. Haben Sie schon dort geschaut?
dialogue.translation: I don't know. Have you already looked there?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ja, aber ich finde ihn nicht.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but I can't find it.

scenario: Ordering a drink at a café
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: used here in the sense of 'preparing' a drink

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Guten Tag! Was möchten Sie trinken?
dialogue.translation: Good day! What would you like to drink?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte. Und ich will noch etwas Wasser.
dialogue.translation: I would like a coffee, please. And I also want some water.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Einen Kaffee mit Milch? Und das Wasser kommt sofort.
dialogue.translation: A coffee with milk? And the water comes right away.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, mit Milch, aber ohne Zucker. Danke!
dialogue.translation: Yes, with milk, but without sugar. Thank you!

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ich mache das sofort.
dialogue.translation: I'll do that right away.

scenario: Buying a ticket at a station
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Indefinite article for feminine nouns, such as 'Fahrkarte' (ticket).
Used with cities without article: 'nach Berlin'.
Form of 'kosten' (to cost) in the 3rd person singular.
Definite article for masculine nouns like 'Zug' (train).
Used to indicate time: 'um 10 Uhr' (at 10 o'clock).
Form of 'können' (can) in the 1st/3rd person singular.
Irregular verb: ich fahre, du fährst.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Guten Tag! Ich möchte eine Fahrkarte nach Berlin, bitte.
dialogue.translation: Good day! I would like a ticket to Berlin, please.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Wie viel kostet der Zug um 10 Uhr?
dialogue.translation: How much does the 10 o'clock train cost?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Und wann kann ich mit dem Zug fahren?
dialogue.translation: And when can I travel by train?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Der Zug um 10 Uhr kostet 20 Euro. Sie können um 10 Uhr fahren.
dialogue.translation: The 10 o'clock train costs 20 euros. You can travel at 10 o'clock.

key_phrases.translation: How much does the train cost?

scenario: Checking in at a hotel reception
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Neuter (das Zimmer). Used for the hotel room.
Takes accusative. E.g.: für eine Nacht = for one night.
Here used as a polite request. (Already common, but essential.)
Indefinite. E.g.: Alles gut? = Everything okay?
Takes accusative or dative. E.g.: an der Rezeption = at the reception.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Guten Abend! Ich habe ein Zimmer für eine Nacht reserviert.
dialogue.translation: Good evening! I reserved a room for one night.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Guten Abend! Ihr Name, bitte?
dialogue.translation: Good evening! Your name, please?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mein Name ist Anna Schmidt. Hier ist mein Pass.
dialogue.translation: My name is Anna Schmidt. Here is my passport.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Danke. Alles ist fertig. Ihr Zimmer ist Nummer 12, an der Rezeption.
dialogue.translation: Thank you. Everything is ready. Your room is number 12, at the reception.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vielen Dank! Auf Wiedersehen!
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much! Goodbye!

scenario: Meeting a new neighbor
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Copular verb, already common at A1.
Adjective used to introduce something recent.
Regular verb, used with the preposition 'in'.
Used with verbs to express liking.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hallo! Ich bin neu hier.
dialogue.translation: Hello! I am new here.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Hallo! Ich wohne auch hier. Wir sind Nachbarn.
dialogue.translation: Hello! I also live here. We are neighbors.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Gern lerne ich Sie kennen, aber ich habe noch keine Zeit.
dialogue.translation: I would be glad to meet you, but I don't have time yet.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Kein Problem. Wir sehen uns später.
dialogue.translation: No problem. We'll see each other later.

key_phrases.translation: I would be glad to meet you.

scenario: Asking the time on the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Used as a way to apologize or politely get someone's attention.
Irregular verb; often used to express possession or state.
Adjective used to indicate lateness or advanced time.
Common interrogative adverb to ask about manner or intensity.
Adverb of quantity, often used in questions about time.
Feminine noun; used to indicate exact hours (e.g., um Uhr).
Temporal adverb indicating sequence or consequence.
Irregular verb; used to indicate movement toward the speaker.
Irregular verb; used to indicate movement in general.
Irregular verb; used for visual perception.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entschuldigung, haben Sie die Uhr?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, do you have the time?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, es ist wie viel Uhr?
dialogue.translation: Yes, what time is it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Es ist schon spät, dann müssen Sie gehen.
dialogue.translation: It's already late, then you must go.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ich sehe, es ist drei Uhr. Danke!
dialogue.translation: I see, it's three o'clock. Thank you!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Bitte, kommen Sie gut nach Hause.
dialogue.translation: You're welcome, get home safely.

key_phrases.translation: Excuse me, do you have the time?

scenario: At the doctor for a basic checkup
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Literally 'practice', but used for doctor's office
In the medical context, it is the medication prescription
Here used as 'to hurt' (e.g., 'Was tut Ihnen weh?')

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Guten Tag, Herr Doktor. Ich fühle mich heute nicht gut.
dialogue.translation: Good day, doctor. I don't feel well today.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Guten Tag. Was tut Ihnen weh?
dialogue.translation: Good day. What hurts?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Mein Kopf tut weh, aber nur ein bisschen.
dialogue.translation: My head hurts, but only a little.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nehmen Sie dieses Medikament, dann sind Sie bald wieder gesund.
dialogue.translation: Take this medication, then you'll be healthy again soon.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Danke. Und bekommen Sie das Rezept für die Praxis?
dialogue.translation: Thank you. And do you get the prescription for the practice?

key_phrases.translation: What hurts? / Where is the pain?

scenario: Paying at a supermarket checkout
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Regular verb, used in the sense of paying a bill.
Here it means payment card, but it can also be map or letter.
Used to affirm; can also be an emphasis particle.
Demonstrative pronoun or neuter definite article; here used as a pronoun.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Guten Tag! Das macht 12 Euro.
dialogue.translation: Good day! That will be 12 euros.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, ich zahle mit Karte oder bar?
dialogue.translation: Yes, do I pay by card or in cash?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Sie können mit Karte oder bar zahlen.
dialogue.translation: You can pay by card or in cash.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Danke, ich zahle bar. Hier ist das Geld.
dialogue.translation: Thank you, I'll pay in cash. Here is the money.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Danke! Sie kaufen heute viel. Auf Wiedersehen!
dialogue.translation: Thank you! You are buying a lot today. Goodbye!

scenario: Calling a friend to make simple plans
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: can be used as adjective or adverb

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hallo Anna, hast du morgen Zeit? Wir können etwas machen.
dialogue.translation: Hello Anna, do you have time tomorrow? We can do something.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, ich habe Zeit. Was willst du machen? Vielleicht ins Kino?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have time. What do you want to do? Maybe go to the cinema?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Gute Idee! Wann treffen wir uns? Um zehn Uhr?
dialogue.translation: Good idea! When do we meet? At ten o'clock?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Um zehn ist gut, aber nicht so früh. Vielleicht um elf?
dialogue.translation: Ten is good, but not so early. Maybe at eleven?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ja, das ist gut. Treffen wir uns am Kino. Bis morgen!
dialogue.translation: Yes, that's good. Let's meet at the cinema. See you tomorrow!

key_phrases.translation: what do you want to do?

scenario: Describing your family to someone
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Used for age: 'Wie alt bist du?'
Regular verb: ich liebe, du liebst.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wer ist das auf dem Foto?
dialogue.translation: Who is that in the photo?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Das ist meine Mutter und das ist mein Vater.
dialogue.translation: That is my mother and that is my father.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Hast du auch einen Bruder oder eine Schwester?
dialogue.translation: Do you also have a brother or a sister?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, ich habe einen kleinen Bruder. Er ist sehr klein.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have a little brother. He is very small.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Wie alt ist er?
dialogue.translation: How old is he?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Er ist drei Jahre alt. Ich liebe ihn sehr.
dialogue.translation: He is three years old. I love him very much.

scenario: Asking for directions in the street
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Indicates going in a straight line.
Indicates a place distant from the speaker.
Here used in 'um die Ecke' = 'around the corner'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Entschuldigung, wo ist die Straße zum Bahnhof?
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, where is the street to the train station?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Gehen Sie geradeaus, dann links und dann rechts um die Ecke.
dialogue.translation: Go straight ahead, then left, and then right around the corner.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Ist es weit?
dialogue.translation: Is it far?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Nein, es ist nicht weit. Dort sehen Sie den Bahnhof.
dialogue.translation: No, it's not far. There you see the train station.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Danke vielmals!
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much!

scenario: On a bus asking the driver for help
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Used for movement in a vehicle; in the present, forms 'fährt'.
Used in polite requests; also means 'you're welcome'.
With 'ein' (get in) or 'aus' (get out); in the present: 'steigt'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bitte, kann ich hier in den Bus steigen?
dialogue.translation: Please, can I get on the bus here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, aber Sie müssen am nächsten Punkt aussteigen.
dialogue.translation: Yes, but you have to get off at the next stop.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Können Sie mir helfen? Ich weiß nicht, wo die Haltestelle ist.
dialogue.translation: Can you help me? I don't know where the stop is.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Der Mann da vorne kann Ihnen helfen. Er fährt den Bus.
dialogue.translation: The man up front can help you. He drives the bus.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Vielen Dank! Dann steige ich hier aus.
dialogue.translation: Thank you very much! Then I'll get off here.

scenario: Introducing a colleague at work
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Regular verb; frequently used in professional contexts.
Adjective; agrees in gender and number with the noun.
Masculine noun (n-declension: den Kollegen, dem Kollegen).
Masculine noun; used in greetings like 'Guten Tag'.
Adjective; also used as an adverb to express satisfaction.
Adverb of inclusion; flexible position in the sentence.
Preposition that governs the dative; used to indicate origin.
Coordinating conjunction; connects words and clauses.

dialogue.translation: Good day, Mrs. Schmidt. This is Mr. Weber, our new colleague.

dialogue.speaker: C

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: Very nice. Mr. Weber, this is Mrs. Schmidt. She works in sales.

scenario: Leaving a voicemail message
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

Modal verb, already used before, but here in a new context.

dialogue.text: Hallo, hier ist Anna. Ich bin nicht zu Hause.
dialogue.translation: Hello, this is Anna. I am not at home.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Bitte rufen Sie später an oder hinterlassen Sie eine Nachricht.
dialogue.translation: Please call later or leave a message.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: B

scenario: At the post office sending a package
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Feminine, used without article in phrases like 'zur Post'
Regular verb, often used with 'an' + person
Regular verb, used with accusative (the price)

Used with verbs like 'bekommen' (to get back)

dialogue.translation: Good day! I would like to send a package.

dialogue.speaker: A

scenario: Asking about opening hours
frequency_note: top 300 most frequent words of German

vocabulary.note: Irregular verb; used for possession and also in time expressions.

Used to indicate the closing of shops or establishments.
Used to indicate the start of a time.
Used to indicate the end of a time.
Used to ask/when something happens late.

Copulative verb; used with adjectives like 'offen' (open) or 'geschlossen' (closed).
